item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q004_ferritin_like_functional_divergence","answer":"SCOPe classifies these as distinct families within the ferritin-like superfamily (SCCS a.25.1): ferritins (a.25.1.1), ribonucleotide-reductase-like proteins (a.25.1.2), and manganese catalases (a.25.1.3), all in the ferritin-like fold (a.25). Thus, SCOPe proposes remote common ancestry—stronger than merely sharing a fold—while the separate families reflect substantial divergence. Their common four-helix-bundle framework and related metal-ligand topology have been adapted to different chemistries: iron oxidation/storage in ferritins, metallocofactor-dependent radical or oxygen chemistry in ribonucleotide-reductase-like proteins, and peroxide disproportionation by manganese catalases. Family membership must not be used to transfer the exact reaction, substrate, metal identity, ligand geometry, oligomeric state, or kinetics. Cross-family structures are reasonable templates for the global core but not for detailed active-site modeling or functional annotation. Such assignments require family-specific sequence/profile support, conservation of catalytic ligands, structural evidence for the active-site environment, metal identification or spectroscopy, and direct biochemical assays.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
